epilogue: The terminal hums where the quiet used to be.

memos.subject: AUTOMATED AUTHORIZATION
memos.text: Your terminal is live. Key the card number as the merchant reads it; read the verdict back. The system is faster than the fiche. Quotas are adjusted accordingly. The terminal is authoritative.

rulebook.text: Decline any card number appearing in the current hot card bulletin.
Decline any charge that would put an account over its credit limit.
A charge at or under floor limit should not be called in. If it is, decline and note it.
Decline the second of two drafts from one merchant on one card within one shift (split draft).
Key every call into the terminal and relay its verdict.

calls.note: Terminal says approve; bulletin №43 lists the card. First machine-vs-desk disagreement.

items.head: MERCHANT NOTICE
items.body: Telephone authorizations will be processed by automated system effective this week. The telephone call is unchanged. Merchants should have the card at hand when calling.

items.head: HOSPITAL NOTES
items.body: Admitted: Mr. O. Higgins. Discharged: Mrs. N. Drodge, Mr. A. Gosse. Visitors 2–4 and 7–8.

items.head: COUNCIL NOTES
items.body: Council heard the wharf crane requires $900 in repairs. The clerk was directed to obtain three prices. The matter of dogs running at large was deferred.

items.head: BIRTHS
items.body: To Mr. and Mrs. E. Grandin, a son. To Mr. and Mrs. R. Strickland, twin daughters. Congratulations.

items.head: FISHERIES REPORT
items.body: Landings steady for the season. Prices unchanged. The plant advises the Saturday shift stands.

items.head: HOCKEY
